author: Bowling Green Today
title: Senator Rand Paul calls for accountability over pardons process and Butler security incident
text:

U.S. Senator Rand Paul | U.S. Senator Rand Paul official website
Senator Rand Paul, a Republican representing Kentucky, addressed issues of government accountability and security in a series of posts on his official Twitter account between July 15 and July 16, 2025.
On July 15, Senator Paul questioned the role of Jeff Zients in presidential pardons and called for greater scrutiny from federal authorities. He wrote, "It’s surprising to learn that Jeff Zients oversaw presidential pardons. We must urge the Department of Justice to take its responsibilities seriously and hold Fauci accountable for his actions. The evidence against him is both clear and substantial. It raises serious questions" (July 15, 2025).
Later that day, Senator Paul commented on policy changes under current leadership compared to previous administrations. In his words: "The previous administration made severe mistakes that must not happen again. Under @POTUS’s leadership, we are confidently seeing a strong return to safety and accountability." (July 15, 2025).
Addressing recent events in Pennsylvania on July 16, Senator Paul criticized the handling of security in Butler: "What happened in Butler was a catastrophic security breakdown. It was a total collapse of planning and communication from D.C. to the rooftop in Butler, PA. You can’t fix this with money. You fix it with accountability. Full breakdown on @DanaLoeschRadio." (July 16, 2025).
Senator Paul's remarks come amid ongoing debates about government oversight following high-profile incidents involving public health officials and security lapses at political events.
